text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPhilosophyThe Quest for Wisdom in Turbulent TimesA conversation with three Harvard professors about the practice of wisdom in everyday livingKFBy Kristen French3:00 PM CDT on October 28, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleFor more than a decade a group of Harvard professors has taught a class about wisdom and its religious, moral, and aesthetic dimensions to undergraduates. The four professors are friends from distinct disciplines:­ Michael Puett, a historian of religions; Arthur Kleinman, a physician and medical anthropologist; Stephanie Paulsell, a theologian and literary scholar; and Davíd Carrasco, a historian and anthropologist.Inside and outside of the classroom, they have sought to understand how their own areas of study might relate to the art of living well and seeking wisdom during both ordinary and extraordinary times. Now they have written a book that outlines some of the insights they have shared with students and what they have learned while teaching the class, The Practice of Wisdom: Five Quests. These quests wind through the labyrinthine challenges of caregiving, solitude, self-understanding, and transcendence. Read more: “What Is Intelligence?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
